idiom_name: when (a) { is Circle -> when (b) { is Square -> ... } }
implementation_notes: Kotlin makes an exhaustive when over a sealed hierarchy a compile-time obligation, which is precisely the safety the visitor provided: nested whens resolve both runtime types and the compiler refuses to build while an arm is missing. What Kotlin does not provide is a tuple type pattern, so the pair decision is composed from two single-axis whens (or from a Pair-keyed table), and an else arm silently restores the old runtime-failure mode. The classic visitor (see classic-visitor) remains the right shape when either hierarchy is open, spread over modules, or part of a public API.
pitfalls: An else branch (or a non-sealed subject) switches off exhaustiveness and reintroduces silent misses.
Sealed subclasses must live in the same module and package: moving one out breaks the compile-time guarantee.
Two nested whens produce N x M arms; extract a Pair-keyed dispatch table once the matrix outgrows a screen.

variants.name: Visitor interface + accept()
variants.idiom_name: ShapeVisitor with visit(c: Circle)/visit(s: Square) + accept
variants.implementation_notes: Kotlin supports method overloading, so the Java-style visitor compiles unchanged: each element implements accept by calling the overload matching its own type and the visitor declares one method per concrete element. It is still the option for open or third-party hierarchies and for operations that need to be units of testing or DI; for closed hierarchies Kotlin's sealed classes plus exhaustive when express the same guarantee with less ceremony, and extension functions often replace visitors whose operations carry no shared state.
pitfalls: A visitor holding mutable state is single-use; Kotlin's data classes make it tempting to reuse it across traversals.
Overload resolution uses the static type of this, so a base-class accept (or an extension function) silently selects the wrong method.
Open instead of sealed element hierarchies remove the compile-time coverage - declare them sealed unless third parties must extend them.
